# Neuroscience Bulletin

[English](https://github.com/Zhang-Zhaoji/scientific-bulletin) [中文](https://github.com/Zhang-Zhaoji/scientific-bulletin/blob/main/README_zh.md)

**Caution: some of the codes are generated by the Kimi K2.5, GPT5.3 codex, GPT5.5, and other leading LLMs, which may include some hallucination.**

Maintainers dedicate the Neuroscience Bulletin repo to be a WeChat public account that looks up recent neuroscience articles and shares them with readers. The repository contains an end-to-end literature curation pipeline:
- 🕷️ Crawl titles, abstracts and metadata from 15+ top neuroscience-related journals and preprint servers
- 🔍 Enrich papers with abstracts, affiliation information and normalized institutions using Europe PMC and ROR (Research Organization Registry)
- 💾 Store all processed data in SQLite database for easy querying and analysis
- 🤖 Score, categorize and summarize papers with LLMs, then generate weekly Markdown and WeChat-style reports
- 📊 Generate data visualizations of global research output, country distribution, institution rankings and paper score statistics

The repository currently includes weekly crawl data, enriched JSONL files, LLM outputs, reports and figures from March to May 2026. The latest local report artifact is generated on **2026-05-24**. Published public-facing content is collected in the Zhihu column "Neuroscience Bulletin": https://www.zhihu.com/column/c_2016331747525157941

This repository contains the code and data of the Neuroscience Bulletin project. We wish to make the project open-source and accessible to everyone. If you have any questions or suggestions, please feel free to contact us.

## 🚀 Quick Start

### Prerequisites

```bash
# Recommended
pip install -r requirements.txt

# Core crawler dependencies
pip install requests beautifulsoup4 jsonlines python-dateutil tqdm selenium

# Enrichment dependencies; SQLite uses Python's built-in sqlite3 module
pip install pandas numpy

# LLM processing dependencies
pip install openai tiktoken

# Visualization dependencies
pip install matplotlib pyecharts snapshot_selenium
```

### Usage

```bash
# Fetch articles from all sources (default last 8 days)
python src/main.py

# Fetch articles, then skip automatic author/ROR enrichment
python src/main.py --no-auto-enrich

# Use more workers for enrichment and check more historical issues for deduplication
python src/main.py --workers 4 --history-weeks 3

# Fetch only from arXiv and bioRxiv (preprints)
python src/main.py --arxiv-only --biorxiv-only

# Fetch from last 14 days instead of 7 (applies to all sources)
python src/main.py --days 14

# Enrich papers with ROR affiliation data
python src/batch_enrich_authors.py

# Build SQLite database from processed papers
python sql_scripts/build_sqlite.py

# Rebuild the full bundled SQLite database from all weekly JSONL/LLM outputs
bashScripts/build_sq.bat

# Generate LLM summaries and reports
python LLM_eval/main.py

# Process a specific enriched JSONL file with a chosen model
python LLM_eval/main.py -i getfiles/all_papers_2026-05-23_enriched_ror_refined.jsonl --model glm-5.1

# Generate data visualizations
python visualize/main.py

# Generate a weekly country heatmap and country distribution pie chart from JSONL
python visualize/global_heatmap.py --jsonl getfiles/all_papers_2026-05-23_enriched_ror_refined.jsonl --date 2026-05-23

# Build a static website from generated Markdown reports
python scripts/build_pages.py --input-dir LLM_Results --output-dir docs
```

See `python src/main.py --help` and `python LLM_eval/main.py --help` for all crawler and LLM options. LLM processing expects `DASHSCOPE_API_KEY` and `API_BASE_URL` to be available in the environment or a `.env` file.

## 📚 Supported Sources

### Preprint Servers ✅

| Source | Status | Description |
|--------|--------|-------------|
| **arXiv** | ✅ Supported | q-bio.NC, q-bio.TO, q-bio.MN categories |
| **bioRxiv** | ✅ Supported | All neuroscience-related preprints |

**Note on arXiv:** Fetches from three core neuroscience categories:
- **q-bio.NC** - Neurons and Cognition (primary neuroscience)
- **q-bio.TO** - Tissues and Organs (neural tissues, brain organoids)
- **q-bio.MN** - Molecular Networks (molecular neuroscience)

### Springer Nature Journals ✅

| Journal | Status |
|---------|--------|
| Nature | ✅ |
| Nature Biomedical Engineering | ✅ |
| Nature Methods | ✅ |
| Nature Neuroscience | ✅ |
| Nature Human Behaviour | ✅ |

### Other Journals ✅

| Journal | Status | Method |
|---------|--------|--------|
| **Science** | ✅ Supported | List pages + Europe PMC enrichment |
| **Science Advances** | ✅ Supported | TOC page + Selenium (date filtered) |
| **PNAS** | ✅ Supported | PubMed API |
| **Cell Press** | ✅ Supported | Selenium + Europe PMC enrichment |
| **Nature Communications** | ✅ Supported | Subject pages (Biological/Health Sciences) |
| **Brain** | ✅ Supported | PubMed API |
| **eLife** | ✅ Supported | PubMed API |
| **Journal of Neurophysiology** | ✅ Supported | PubMed (primary) + Europe PMC (supplementary) |
| **Journal of Neuroscience** | ✅ Supported | PubMed API (filters Journal Club articles by default) |
| **Journal of Cognitive Neuroscience** | ✅ Supported | PubMed API |
| **Journal of Vision** | ✅ Supported | PubMed API |

### Cell Press Journals ✅

| Journal | Status | Method |
|---------|--------|--------|
| **Cell** | ✅ Supported | Current issue page + Europe PMC enrichment |
| **Neuron** | ✅ Supported | Current issue page + Europe PMC enrichment |
| **Current Biology** | ✅ Supported | Current issue page + Europe PMC enrichment |
| **Trends in Neurosciences** | ✅ Supported | Current issue page + Europe PMC enrichment |

**Note on Science:** Uses a smart enrichment strategy:
1. Fetch basic info from Science list pages (no captcha)
2. Enrich with Europe PMC via DOI (abstract, PMID, etc.)
3. Fallback to preprint servers (bioRxiv/arXiv) if not in Europe PMC
4. Keep original data if nothing is found

## 🔬 Data Enrichment

### Metadata Enrichment

| Service | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| **Europe PMC** | Primary enrichment source (PubMed abstracts, PMC full-text, PMID/PMCID) |
| **Preprint Fallback** | Search bioRxiv/arXiv for preprint versions of published papers |

### ROR Affiliation Enrichment ✅

We use the Research Organization Registry (ROR) to normalize author affiliation information:
- Normalize institution names to standard ROR identifiers
- Extract country/region information for all authors
- Generate statistics on global research output distribution
- Support for batch processing of large paper datasets
- Support integrated crawler-time enrichment with configurable worker count and ROR matching threshold

### Deduplication and Recheck

The main crawler can merge sources and remove duplicates by DOI, PMID and normalized title. It also checks recent historical issues so already-covered papers are not repeated, while papers that were previously missing abstracts can be rechecked in later runs.

---

## 💾 SQLite Database

All processed papers are stored in a SQLite database for efficient querying and analysis:
- Schema supports all paper metadata, enrichment information and affiliation data
- Fast querying by date, source, journal, country, and keywords
- Integrated with visualization and LLM processing modules
- Automatic deduplication of papers from multiple sources

---

## 🤖 LLM Analysis & Report Generation

We use OpenAI-compatible LLM APIs to process collected papers:
- **Default processing model**: `glm-5.1` in `LLM_eval/main.py`
- **Report polishing model used by report scripts**: `qwen3.6-flash-2026-04-16`
- **Core Functions**:
  - Classify papers as core neuroscience, high-impact cross-domain work, limited cross-domain work, or out-of-scope work
  - Score eligible papers with structured criteria and assign recommendation tiers
  - Summarize paper abstracts into concise, easy-to-understand highlights
  - Categorize papers by research topic and cross-domain tags
  - Generate weekly research reports for WeChat public account and Zhihu
  - Support custom prompt templates for different use cases
- **Outputs**: Structured JSON analysis results, formatted Markdown reports and WeChat-formatted Markdown reports

---

## 📊 Data Visualization

Built-in visualization module for analyzing research trends:
- **Global Heatmap**: Visualize research output distribution by country/region
- **Country Distribution Pie Chart**: Show proportion of papers from different countries
- **Paper Score Histogram**: Statistical distribution of paper influence metrics
- **Institution Ranking**: Generate top institution tables for the report period
- **Report Statistics Text**: Insert country, institution and score summaries into generated Markdown reports
- **Output Formats**: Static PNG images, interactive HTML charts
- **Weekly Country View**: `visualize/global_heatmap.py --jsonl ... --date ...` can render a country heatmap and country distribution pie chart directly from a weekly JSONL file
- All visualizations are automatically generated as part of the weekly pipeline

---

## 🌐 Static Website / GitHub Pages

Reports can be published as standalone HTML pages so the layout is not constrained by Zhihu or WeChat formatting rules.

- `scripts/build_pages.py` converts `LLM_Results/report_*.md` into a static site under `docs/`
- Report pages embed matching cover images, country heatmaps and country distribution charts from `Imgs/`
- The index page includes a compact cover thumbnail for each report
- The GitHub Actions workflow `.github/workflows/pages.yml` builds and deploys the site to GitHub Pages on pushes to `main`; it can enable Pages automatically when the repository is configured for GitHub Actions Pages deployments
- The builder uses the Python `markdown` package with table/list extensions, so inline Markdown such as `**bold**` and Markdown tables are rendered as real HTML
- If local rendering fails with a missing dependency, run `python -m pip install markdown` or `pip install -r requirements.txt`

## 🔧 Development

### Testing Individual Crawlers

```bash
# Test arXiv crawler
python src/crawler_arxiv.py

# Test bioRxiv crawler
python src/crawler_biorxiv.py
```

### Adding a New Journal

1. Check if the journal provides an API or RSS feed
2. Create a new crawler file in `src/crawler_<journal>.py`
3. Implement the following interface:
   - `fetch_papers()`: Returns list of paper dicts with keys: `title`, `authors`, `date`, `url`, `abstract`
   - `save_papers()`: Saves to JSONL file
4. Add the crawler to `src/main.py`

---

## 📖 Data Format

Articles are saved in JSONL format with the following fields (enriched versions have additional fields):

```json
{
  "type": "Article",
  "title": "Paper title",
  "authors": ["Author 1", "Author 2", "..."],
  "affiliations": ["Institution 1, Country 1", "..."],
  "ror_ids": ["https://ror.org/xxxxxx", "..."],
  "countries": ["Country 1", "..."],
  "date": "DD MMM YYYY",
  "url": "https://...",
  "abstract": "Paper abstract...",
  "source": "arXiv|bioRxiv|Nature|...",
  "pdf_url": "https://... (optional)",
  "doi": "10.xxxx/... (optional)",
  "pmid": "xxxxxx (optional)",
  "pmcid": "PMCxxxxxx (optional)"
}
```

---

## ⚠️ Notes

### Rate Limiting

- **arXiv**: No strict rate limits, but please be respectful (1s delay between requests)
- **bioRxiv**: No rate limits documented
- **Nature/Science**: May require delays and user-agent rotation
- **LLM APIs**: Follow rate limits for respective model providers

### Anti-Bot Protection

Some publishers (Science, Cell/Elsevier) use Cloudflare or similar protection. Our approach:

1. **Preferred**: Use official APIs when available (arXiv, bioRxiv, PubMed)
2. **Alternative**: Use PubMed/Europe PMC for journal articles
3. **Last resort**: Selenium with manual captcha solving
